newsitem.title: USA: Barnes & Noble encouraged by online sales.
newsitem.headline: Barnes & Noble encouraged by online sales.

text.p: Barnes & Noble Inc said on Thursday it was encouraged by early sales trends from its new Internet business.
Barnes & Noble went online with its own Web site last week as its rival Amazon.com Inc went public. The two companies have clashed over the title of world's largest bookseller.
Barnes & Noble on Thursday reported a net loss of $0.12 per share, but said it had an operating profit for the first time since it began its "super store" expansion.

"We are also encouraged by early sales trends from our online business in America Online's Marketplace and our new World Wide Web site," company Chairman Leonard Riggio said in a news release. "Since we launched this business, the number of online transactions has been increasing daily."

The operating profit of $3.1 million compared to an operating loss of $0.1 million for the same period the year before. Super store revenues were up 26.3 percent, accounting for 81 percent of total revenue.
Barnes & Noble shares were up 7/8 to 42-3/8 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
